  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "The 'Combined' paradigm contains nearly half of all trials, which may dominate aggregate means and obscure specific effects if not analyzed via group-level comparisons.",
    "The 'Sham' and 'Bright Visual Only' paradigms have substantially fewer samples (n=3,505 and n=3,323 respectively) compared to others, increasing the uncertainty of their marginal means.",
    "Without group-specific means and standard errors, it is impossible to determine which paradigm yields the fastest time-to-target, highest success, or most efficient path.",
    "The extreme ranges in Time-to-Target (up to 201.4) and Path Efficiency (up to 29.8) suggest potential outliers or highly heterogeneous performance within specific paradigms."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "While aggregate statistics describe the overall distribution of navigation performance, the provided data summary lacks the necessary group-level breakdowns (means and variances per paradigm) to determine which stimulation strategy is most effective.   ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Perform a one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis test for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the independent factor, using the raw dataset to calculate group means, standard errors, and effect sizes to identify specific paradigm differences."
